qs.q:
Railway Experiences — Which person…

A=Alec (ill, against doctor's advice, repeat trip, everything changed/same, missed adventure, got off, flew home)
B=Brooke (missed train, stayed positive, caught next, daydreamed, interviewer also late)

E=Ellis (packed commuter train, teenagers took seats, sick of commuting, decided to change life)
F=Francesca (born in London, returned after years abroad, underground felt strange, felt like another country)

0. had wanted to buy a book? [D=Daniel: 'returning home after a day searching the bookshops']
1. had to change trains?
2. had a lot of luggage?
3. missed their train?
4. made their journey after dark?
5. fell asleep?
6. did not have a seat?
7. was homesick?
8. did some work on their journey?
9. felt like a tourist?
10. changed their mind?
11. was on their regular journey?
12. was travel sick?
items: 8 — did some work on their journey?

qs.q:
Giant-Man Stanley Cook

"He was free to travel since he didn't have a home of his own or anything to keep him where he was. And he was a happy, well-adjusted chap. He liked to talk to the public and see them enjoy themselves."

What was his main reason for joining a circus?
A It gave him the chance to travel.
B He didn't have a home.
C He needed the money.
D He enjoyed entertaining people.
opts: It gave him the chance to travel.

qs.q:
Giant-Man Stanley Cook

"He was said to stand 7ft 4in tall, and the attention he received from the press and public was his first indication that his unusual height might be a means to make a living."

He realized that he could make money out of his height…
A when he was in care.
B while he was in Canada.
C during a royal celebration.
D at Chigwell.

Giant-Man Stanley Cook

"'His height could be seen as a blessing,' said Jim Cook, 'because it gave him a life he could never otherwise have enjoyed.'"

How did he feel about his height?
A It did not trouble him.
B He felt he was a freak.
C He thought people laughed at him.
D He was grateful for it.
opts: He felt he was a freak.
He thought people laughed at him.

qs.q:
Giant-Man Stanley Cook

"'He just wanted to bring in the crowds.' Stanley claimed he was 8ft 4in and continued to do so for the rest of his life."

His manager…
A lied to him.
B exploited him.
C treated him fairly.
D treated him like a member of the family.
opts: treated him like a member of the family.

qs.q:
Giant-Man Stanley Cook

"'I'd say that its role in helping me RECONNECT WITH FAMILY has been its GREATEST GIFT to me.'"

Jim Cook is particularly appreciative of the fact that…
A he has found out about his family.
B he has had the chance to travel.
C he has received money for his work.
D he has revived the memory of his great-uncle.
opts: he has found out about his family.
he has had the chance to travel.
he has received money for his work.
he has revived the memory of his great-uncle.

The desire to define ourselves

"Personality fascinates and challenges us. (19) ___. Meanwhile, our identity and relation to the world is defined in the categories psychologists have identified."

A They tended to define personality purely as a potentiality to behave in a certain way.
B Aside from the satisfaction of cracking the code, the aim was to predict human behaviour.
C If we could sample language, we could build a complete lexicon of human personality traits.
D Psychologists and scientists have devoted themselves to understanding it for more than a century.
E A child is born with strikingly recognisable traits, many different from their parents.
F They make us the individuals that we are, but also unpredictable.
G Each trait indicates or predicts the way you may behave in certain situations.
H It shows that we have several personalities, depending on the situation.
opts: A — Defined personality purely as potentiality to behave in a certain way.
B — Aim was to predict human behaviour.
C — Could build a complete lexicon of personality traits.
D — Psychologists devoted themselves to understanding it for more than a century.
E — A child is born with strikingly recognisable traits.
F — They make us individuals, but also unpredictable.
G — Each trait predicts the way you may behave.
H — We have several personalities depending on situation.
